title: Streaming upload endpoint to disk with quotas
when: A Node API must accept uploads of many megabytes, write them to disk without holding them in memory, enforce size and per user quotas and never leave partial files behind.
prompt:
Goal: POST /uploads streams the raw body into a temp file with a byte cap and checksum, then moves it into storage atomically.
Steps:
1. Clients send the file as the raw body with Content-Type and an X-File-Name header; keep multipart only for plain HTML form posts.
2. Refuse early: Content-Length over the cap gives 413; a user whose stored total plus this size passes the quota gets 413 with code quota_exceeded.
3. await pipeline(req, capBytes(max), hashTap, createWriteStream(tmp, { flags: "wx" })), where capBytes is a Transform that errors past max and hashTap feeds createHash("sha256").
4. Keep tmp on the same volume (storage/tmp/<uuid>) so the final fs.rename is atomic.
5. In finally, on any error or client abort, unlink the temp file and reply 413, 400 or 500.
6. On success rename to storage/files/<uuid>, insert { id, owner, size, sha256, type, originalName } and reply 201 with Location.
Quality bar:
- Memory stays flat for a 1 GB upload.
- At most N uploads run per user at once.
- Startup deletes temp files older than an hour.
Pitfalls:
- req.on("data") pushing chunks into an array.
- Writing to the final path directly, leaving broken files on abort.
- Using the client file name in the path.
Verify:
- [ ] An oversized upload stops at the cap and leaves no file.
- [ ] An aborted upload leaves no temp file.
- [ ] Rows store size and sha256.
- [ ] 201 has Location.
Output: routes/uploads.mjs, storage layout notes in README.md, test/uploads.test.mjs.

examples.input: upload de videos de 500 MB estoura a memoria do servidor
examples.output: pipeline to storage/tmp with byte cap and sha256, atomic rename, quota check, cleanup on abort
